title: Works of mercy for the soul
word: Works of mercy for the soul
hookLine: teach, counsel, correct gently, comfort, forgive, bear wrongs, pray

cards: Job has lost nearly everything: his children, his wealth, his health. He sits in the ashes. Three friends travel to see him, and when they arrive they barely recognize him.

They weep, they tear their robes, and then they do something remarkable: "they sat down with him upon the ground seven days and seven nights, and none spake a word unto him: for they saw that his grief was very great."
A week of silence, side by side in the dirt. It may be the best thing they ever did for him. Because then the talking started.

teach.b: Christian tradition keeps a second list of mercy, for the heart and mind, and each item is done with words, or with holding words back. Teach someone who doesn't know. Counsel someone who doubts.
Correct someone gently. Comfort the sorrowful. Forgive.
Bear wrongs patiently. Pray for others. Correcting comes with a warning label.

Paul writes, "if a man be overtaken in a fault, ye which are spiritual, restore such an one in the spirit of meekness; considering thyself, lest thou also be tempted." Restore, not crush; you could be next.
Comfort, in Paul, travels in a circle: God "comforteth us in all our tribulation, that we may be able to comfort them which are in any trouble." Now back to Job.
After the silence, Job speaks first, cursing the day he was born.
Then his friends answer, and for chapter after chapter they explain his suffering to him. You must have done something. Confess it.
God is punishing you. They meant to counsel and correct. But at the end of the book God says to one of them, "ye have not spoken of me the thing that is right, as my servant Job hath."
That's the warning built into these works: the same sentence can heal or wound. The friends were best when they were silent and present, so the tradition pairs these works with patience and humility.

On the last item, churches differ: Catholic and Orthodox Christians pray for the living and the dead; Protestant churches have taught differently about prayer for the dead, and differ among themselves.
Prayer for the living is shared.

how: Christians practice the works of mercy for the soul, often called the spiritual works of mercy, through teaching, counseling, comforting the grieving, forgiving and praying for others; Catholic and Orthodox Christians include prayer for the dead.

games.q: what does “works of mercy for the soul” mean?
o: the rules for confession before communion
private prayers to save your own soul first
teaching, comforting, forgiving: care by word

games.q: mercy with words — tap the pairs.
p: sat a week and said nothing
restore in the spirit of meekness

s: Job's friends helped him most with their advice
at the end God says they had not spoken the thing that is right. they were best when they sat in silence.
Paul says to correct a person in a spirit of meekness
"restore such an one in the spirit of meekness; considering thyself."
all churches pray for the dead

games.q: you're one of Job's friends. you've traveled far, and you find him in the ashes, barely recognizable. what do you do first?
o: explain why this might have happened.
sit with him on the ground and say nothing.
urge him to confess what he did wrong.
games.why: they sit with him seven days and seven nights, and none speaks a word, "for they saw that his grief was very great." the trouble starts when they begin to talk.

practice: Ask yourself the list as questions, who needs teaching, comfort, gentle correction, forgiveness, prayer, and when one person rises, sit with them in silence for a while, the way Job's friends did at first.
If you pray, you can pray for them now. And if the grief is your own and it has gotten very dark, in the US you can call or text 988, or reach local emergency help.

wordCard.voice: Works of mercy for the soul. Teach, counsel, correct gently, comfort, forgive, bear wrongs, and pray for others.

orig.note: Greek: comfort, encouragement. The comfort word in 2 Corinthians 1.

carryVoice: Your line: mercy with words. Sometimes it starts as silence. Go gently.
